newsitem.title: FRANCE: One Mitterrand staffer slanders other, court rules.
newsitem.headline: One Mitterrand staffer slanders other, court rules.

text.p: In a murky dispute among men who served the late President Francois Mitterrand, a French court rejected as slander on Tuesday accusations by one of them that another was responsible for the death of a third.

The court ordered former gendarmerie officer Paul Barril to pay damages and a fine for a book published last September which blamed Gilles Menage, a presidential aide, for the 1994 death of Mitterrand's confidant Francois de Grossouvre.

Grossouvre was officially judged a suicide. But Barril, who served in Mitterrand's anti-terrorism unit, wrote in "Guerres Secretes a l'Elysee" (Secret Wars at the Elysee) that he had been persecuted by Menage and probably murdered.
The court ordered Barril, jointly with publisher Albin Michel, to pay 200,000 francs ($34,700) in damages to Menage. It also fined Barril 50,000 francs ($8,700).

In a separate judgement, Barril was fined 20,000 francs ($3,400) and ordered to pay 30,000 francs ($5,200) in damages to Menage for similar statements on France-Info radio. He was cleared in a third judgement concerning an article in the magazine L'Express.
